title: HTTP 403 from a limit check during two identity changes
telemetry: Protected fixture reads of Cloud Run service and revision descriptions and of Cloud Logging (container logs, Cloud Audit Logs Admin Activity and Data Access entries), plus a supplied change calendar, dated IAM inventory and caller excerpt; no IAM policy, token or object-content reads.
owner: Avery (Credit on-call); Sam (cloud IAM and audit-log configuration owner); Taylor (owner of bucket creditline-limits-prod and CHG-5530); Jordan (limit-gateway release owner, CHG-5521); Morgan (owner of credit-limit-check and limit-recalc). ITO coordinates the existing TLC.
task: Investigate the HTTP 403 responses limit-gateway has received from credit-limit-check since 09:55:12 UTC. Return a technical finding to Avery that identifies the supported failure boundary, the evidence and unknowns, and a scoped next check for the responsible owner. Make no changes.
common_evidence:
[UNTRUSTED] Supplied synthetic change calendar, identity inventory and caller observations; all principals, resources and identifiers are fictional.
Record cut: 2026-10-15T10:10:00Z; all timestamps are UTC on 2026-10-15 unless stated.
Receiving service: projects/synthetic-creditline-prod/locations/us-central1/services/credit-limit-check.
Callers in the same project: limit-gateway (Cloud Run service) calls POST /v1/check once per incoming order and sends its request ID in the X-Request-Id header; limit-recalc (Cloud Run service) calls POST /v1/check at the start of each minute with request IDs of the form lr-HHMM. Both attach a Google-signed ID token for the receiving service URL.
Application contract (Morgan): credit-limit-check performs no caller-identity check of its own and relies on Cloud Run's invoker check. Each handled /v1/check first reads the metadata of gs://creditline-limits-prod/limits/current.json with the service's runtime identity, then answers. A Cloud Storage authorization failure is returned to the caller as HTTP 403.
Identity inventory captured by Sam at 2026-10-14T18:00:00Z and not refreshed since: credit-limit-check runtime identity limit-reader@synthetic-creditline-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com; service-level roles/run.invoker members serviceAccount:limit-gateway@synthetic-creditline-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and serviceAccount:limit-recalc@synthetic-creditline-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com; bucket creditline-limits-prod roles/storage.objectViewer member serviceAccount:limit-reader@synthetic-creditline-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
Change calendar, 09:50-10:00: CHG-5521 (Jordan) moves limit-gateway to a dedicated identity, limit-gateway-v2@synthetic-creditline-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com, by deploying a new revision; listed prerequisite: roles/run.invoker for the new identity on credit-limit-check. CHG-5530 (Taylor) moves readers of bucket creditline-limits-prod from direct bindings to the group creditline-limit-readers@example.com; listed prerequisite: existing readers added to the group. Completion of neither prerequisite is recorded in this packet.
Caller observations (limit-gateway, Avery's excerpt): 09:54:17.458 request_id=lg-a8e7 order=ORD-88209 status=200; 09:54:47.902 request_id=lg-a8f2 order=ORD-88210 status=200; 09:55:12.281 request_id=lg-a913 order=ORD-88211 status=403; 09:55:41.806 request_id=lg-a92c order=ORD-88212 status=403; 09:56:15.157 request_id=lg-a951 order=ORD-88213 status=403. Every limit check from limit-gateway since 09:55:12 has returned 403, and 26 orders were held awaiting a limit check at 10:08:00.
Receiver request log (Avery's excerpt): a resource.type="cloud_run_revision" request entry with status 403 exists for each of the three failed calls above, within 0.1 s of the caller timestamps; the excerpt retains only timestamp and status.
Network: caller and receiver are in the same project; no VPC Service Controls perimeter is configured for this project.
Avery owns impact on the existing ITO-coordinated TLC; Sam owns IAM and audit-log configuration; Taylor owns bucket creditline-limits-prod and CHG-5530; Jordan owns limit-gateway releases and CHG-5521; Morgan owns credit-limit-check, limit-recalc and their logging.
Tokens, headers other than X-Request-Id, IAM policy documents and object contents are excluded from the packet. No subsequent successful limit check from limit-gateway or recovery record has been supplied.
competing_lead: Two coincident changes, both on the shared change calendar, point at opposite boundaries. CHG-5521 moved limit-gateway to identity limit-gateway-v2@ in revision limit-gateway-00113-qaz, which took traffic at 09:55:06, six seconds before the first 403; the dated inventory lists only the old identity as an invoker, and gateway-revision, gateway-container-logs and admin-activity-audit all show the switch. That is the competing lead in variant B. CHG-5530 removed limit-reader@'s direct objectViewer binding on the bucket at 09:53:40, about 92 seconds before the first 403 and within typical IAM propagation time, in favour of a group whose membership no read shows; admin-activity-audit shows it, and the application maps storage denials to 403. That is the competing lead in variant A, where an hourly storage.objects.list denial for a different principal (limits-export@) in storage-data-access-audit adds a further storage-denial lure. Only the receiver's container log and the Cloud Storage Data Access entries, aligned with the caller's request IDs and times, separate the boundaries; in variant C both return no entries for the window, so both leads stay open.

sources.claim: A Cloud Run HTTP 403 can occur when the principal that generated the token lacks run.routes.invoke; a 403 with a cloud_run_revision log entry is handled as an invoker problem, while one without such an entry may be VPC Service Controls. The page does not document the request-log text or fields for an invoker refusal, so the fixture's request-log excerpt keeps only timestamp and status, and 'refused before the container' is an inference that is not graded as documented wording.

Cloud Run's audit-logged methods include google.cloud.run.v2.Services.UpdateService and Services.SetIamPolicy as ADMIN_WRITE (Admin Activity); the page does not mention service invocations or run.routes.invoke, so the case offers no audit read of invocation decisions; it does not claim that invocations are never audit-logged.
Cloud Run enforces the invoker IAM check by default; it is disabled with the run.googleapis.com/invoker-iam-disabled annotation; invoke access is granted per service with roles/run.invoker.
A calling Cloud Run service's service account needs roles/run.invoker on the receiving service, and the caller fetches a Google-signed ID token whose audience is the receiving service URL.

The service identity is the account running code uses for Google Cloud API calls through Application Default Credentials; it is set per revision and is distinct from the deployer unless configured the same.

Cloud Storage Data Access audit logs are disabled by default and written only when enabled; getting object metadata is DATA_READ, and setting bucket IAM policies is Admin Activity. The page does not list methodName strings or a policy-delta field, so the fixture's storage.objects.get, storage.objects.list and storage.setIamPermissions names and its compiled binding changes are not graded.

Admin Activity audit logs are always written; Data Access audit logs are disabled by default except for BigQuery; the log names are cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity and %2Fdata_access; for read-only requests denied permission, the caller's principal may be redacted unless it is a service account.

Audit entries carry authenticationInfo.principalEmail, authorizationInfo entries with resource, permission and granted, methodName, resourceName and status. The fixture's 'PERMISSION_DENIED (code 7)' status rendering is not documented on this page and is not graded.
storage.objects.get permits reading object data and metadata; storage.objects.list permits listing objects in a bucket.
Allow policy changes typically take effect within 2 minutes, potentially 7 minutes or longer; group membership changes typically take several minutes, potentially hours.

Cloud Run request logs and container logs are separate; cloud_run_revision carries service_name, revision_name, location and project_id labels. The container stdout log name used in the fixture filter is not stated on this page and is not graded.
